issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) — acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int) — but the provided implementation and example calls use a three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch will confuse students about the expected method signature and parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement/UML to require acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (remove the supplier-name parameter), or (B) change the implementation (and example Main call) to accept the supplier name as the first String parameter (e.g., acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)) and handle/ignore the supplierName as appropriate.
